title: Parking Aid Camera: What the Rear View Tells You
introduction:
The lines on the rear-camera picture are not there to decorate the dashboard. I read them as alignment help, then look separately at any highlighted object-alert zone. Those are different messages, and mixing them up makes a useful display needlessly confusing.

For a Mustang equipped with the parking aid camera, this overview explains what the display features mean and how the camera communicates. The camera provides a visual aid when reversing or reverse parking; its operating controls and diagnostic checks have their own instructions.

edits.text: Understanding the rear parking aid camera

The rear parking aid camera provides a visual aid when you reverse or reverse park the vehicle. When you select reverse gear, the rear video camera image can appear on the 8 in (203 mm) touchscreen or the 4.2 in (107 mm) centerstack infotainment display, depending on the vehicle’s equipment.

Fixed and active guidelines overlay the video image to help you align the vehicle. The system also includes manual zoom. Its visual alert function works with the rear audible parking aid system: when an object is detected, it highlights a zone in the video image showing where that detection occurred.

The rear parking aid camera communicates with the BCM through a LIN (local interconnect network) circuit.
edits.why: I keep the questions separate: the guidelines help me understand vehicle alignment, while the highlighted zone marks where an object has been detected. The LIN connection is the communication link between the camera and the BCM.
